answer.rationale: Write-path p99 rose shortly after a release and during settlement peak, so a bad build and insufficient write headroom are both plausible. Rollback is the leading intended fix because the timing aligns with the new release and prior rollback restored a stable write path, but that is not confirmed and a capacity shortfall remains possible. Circuit breaking is rejected because failing settlement writes would violate the no-lost-writes objective. Failover and replica routing are weaker fits without a regional or read-query signal. Verify b1 and b3, then roll back only in a small guarded cohort so peak settlement value is not broadly put at risk if the release is not causal.
